A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work. The main text, equations, algorithms, references, and appendices A–D are readable and matchable; v4's added figures and checklist are also available for inspection.

before.justification: V3 reports mathematical derivations, convergence proofs, and an analytical Gaussian example. Neither its main text nor appendices report original experimental or simulation outcomes.

after.justification: V4 Section 7 and Figure 3 report original Gaussian and mixture-based sampling experiments, including divergence estimates using 1000 independent samples.

M1.justification: Algorithms 1–2, the KL objective, covariance terms, and continuous SGD/SVRG flows retain the same procedures. V4 clarifies sampled-index notation and practical Langevin connections without introducing a new method component.

E1.justification: V4 introduces actual numerical evaluation on two-dimensional Gaussian and mixture-based sampling problems, whereas v3 contains only an analytical Gaussian example. The mixture experiment uses component densities that are equal-weight mixtures of two Gaussians, extending evaluation beyond the closed-form example.

E2.justification: Section 7 and Figure 3 introduce measured three-way comparisons of LD, SGLD, and SVRGLD, corresponding to Riemannian GD, SGD, and SVRG. V3 compares theoretical convergence and complexity but contains no measured comparator results.

E3.justification: V4 establishes the first empirical protocols: dimension 2, finite-sum sizes N=100 for Gaussian and N=5 for mixture experiments, and KL/Fisher divergence evaluated against update steps and gradient computations. Gaussian results use closed-form calculations; mixture results use discrete algorithms and density estimation from 1000 samples.

E4.justification: The analytical Gaussian example and its demonstration of zero SVRG gradient variance are retained. The new experiments are primary performance comparisons; no distinct component ablations, sensitivity sweeps, distribution-shift tests, or error analyses are introduced.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seeds, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. V4's 1000 independent samples specify the density-estimation sample size, not repeated experimental runs; its checklist supplies no additional uncertainty information.

E6.justification: Figure 3 adds eight panels of empirical KL/Fisher divergence curves for the three methods across two targets and two budget measures. These include SVRGLD's pronounced advantage per gradient computation on the Gaussian target. V3 has no corresponding empirical results, so these are additions rather than same-setting performance improvements.

T1.justification: V4 adds a claimed bounded-variance relaxation in Remark 2 and weakens Theorem 3 to require Lipschitz gradients without Lipschitz log densities. Appendix Theorem 4's time scaling and several proof coefficients or time indices are revised. The main rate orders and proof architecture remain, and Appendix Theorem 6 still invokes the stronger Assumption 2.

C1.justification: The principal contributions remain constructing continuous Wasserstein SGD/SVRG flows through Euclidean SDE approximations, linking them to Langevin methods, and establishing convergence rates matching Euclidean counterparts. The rewritten abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain these claims.

C2.justification: V4 acknowledges that Gaussian Example 1 violates the original log-density Lipschitz condition and invokes weaker assumptions, whereas v3 says the assumptions are satisfied. It also qualifies the manifold analogy and Brownian-motion discussion, expands the flows' usefulness for analyzing discrete algorithms, and revises the stated regime where SVRG improves computational complexity.

D1.justification: Section 7 newly specifies random Gaussian means, identity covariances, equal mixture weights, and the 1000-sample density-estimation procedure. Reproducibility remains incomplete: the estimator citation is empty, concrete experimental step sizes are unspecified, and no implementation access or hardware details are provided.

R1.justification: V4 adds Du, Hu, and Lee (2018) and Ren and Wang (2024), and explicitly credits the retained gradient-flow convergence theorem to Chewi (2023). It also refines comparisons with earlier continuous optimization frameworks; the overall related-work coverage remains similar.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work, preliminaries, method explanations, and conclusion are extensively rewritten. Many displayed equations become inline expressions, affiliations and publication headers change, and an experiments section and NeurIPS checklist are added. The proof appendices retain their basic organization.

P2.justification: V4 adds a Riemannian GD schematic, a diagram connecting discrete and continuous dynamics, and the eight-panel experimental Figure 3; v3 has no figures. Text wraps around the explanatory diagrams, equations are reformatted, and algorithm placement and surrounding layout change.

improvement.justification: Compared with v3's theory-only presentation, v4 adds useful diagrams, numerical checks, and acknowledgement of the Gaussian assumption problem. However, the new bounded-variance relaxation lacks a corresponding revised proof, and Theorem 3's weaker assumptions are not reflected in Appendix Theorem 6. Experimental step sizes and the density estimator remain unspecified, while the added checklist marks experimental items NA. These gains and unresolved theoretical and reporting inconsistencies prevent a reliable net quality judgment.
